items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: How did that – what did you do with them?

That was with Bill Stanley, Bunny Barron, Arnold – Arnie, a trombone player. I’ll get it. I’ll think of his last name – and Dick Berg. We were playing one time. We were doing a children’s concert. We were working for young audiences. Usually we – Bill Stanley was the spokesman for the group. He was explaining to the children that you hear marches and things, but there are little melodies within these things and maybe you can identify them. He said, “In the Sousa march, the Stars and Stripes, there’s a bugle

call.” He would say, “And the bugle call goes like this,” and one of us would stand up and play [Wilder sings the melody]. One day, at one school, I would play it, and the next school, Bunny would play it, or vice versa. One of us would play it. So when he said that, Bunny Barron looks – he thinks I’m going to play it, because I grab my trumpet and he grabbed his. I thought he’s going to play it. So we both put the trumpets back, and we’re sitting. We hadn’t played a note. Bill Stanley said – he’s got his back to…
